lines.text: // ryoku-docker provisions the container runtime behind the stash "Cobalt engine"
// switch: it enables docker.service and drives the single ryoku-cobalt container.
// Authorized without a password so the setup wizard is one click rather than a
// password prompt per step, and so the feature works in the session the user is
// already in: every privileged action runs here as root through pkexec, so the
// user's session is never added to the docker group (which would be passwordless
// root for every process they run).
// Scoped to exactly /usr/bin/ryoku-docker for an active local user in the wheel
// group. The passwordless grant stays safe because the helper exposes NO docker
// passthrough: every container action is a fixed argument vector with a
// hardcoded image and container name, and the single caller-supplied value (the
// port) is range-checked to an integer 1024-65535 before anything escalates. A
// helper that forwarded caller flags to `docker run` would be a root hole via
// `-v /:/host`, so it deliberately does not.
// /usr/bin is pinned on purpose: granting a user-writable path (a ~/.local/bin
// copy, say) would let the user rewrite the privileged binary.
polkit.addRule(function (action, subject) {
if (action.id === "org.freedesktop.policykit.exec" &&
action.lookup("program") === "/usr/bin/ryoku-docker" &&
subject.local && subject.active && subject.isInGroup("wheel")) {
return polkit.Result.YES;
# Maono USB mics (PD400X, DM30, ...) expose gain, EQ, compressor, limiter and
# the monitor mix on a vendor-defined HID page rather than the audio interface.
# The kernel leaves that node root-only, so grant the active-session user access
# (uaccess, no group setup) and any control app can reach it.
KERNEL=="hidraw*", ATTRS{idVendor}=="352f", TAG+="uaccess"
SUBSYSTEM=="usb", ATTR{idVendor}=="352f", TAG+="uaccess"
// Ryoku: let the desktop user (in the wheel group) restart bluetooth.service
// without a password prompt. ryoku-bluetooth-reset.service uses this once the
// session audio stack is up, to clear the BlueZ 5.83+ regression (bluez#1545)
// where an A2DP device disconnects ~1s after connecting and stays broken until
// the bluetooth service is restarted. Scoped to the single manage-units action
// on bluetooth.service; no other privilege is granted. Installed to
// /usr/share/polkit-1/rules.d/ by the ryoku-desktop package.
polkit.addRule(function (action, subject) {
if (action.id === "org.freedesktop.systemd1.manage-units" &&
action.lookup("unit") === "bluetooth.service" &&
subject.isInGroup("wheel")) {
return polkit.Result.YES;
# Grant the active-session user access to /dev/i2c-* so ddcutil (brightness over
# DDC/CI) works without adding users to the i2c group.
SUBSYSTEM=="i2c-dev", GROUP="i2c", MODE="0660", TAG+="uaccess"
# Let the video group write panel brightness without a logind seat. On ASUS
# AMD+NVIDIA laptops the panel backlight (amdgpu_bl0, revealed by
# acpi_backlight=native) is root:root with no seat ACL, so ryoku-cmd-brightness'
# direct sysfs writes fail; chgrp/chmod for the video group (chroot.sh adds the
# user to it) lets brightnessctl set brightness without going through logind.
ACTION=="add", SUBSYSTEM=="backlight", RUN+="/usr/bin/chgrp video /sys/class/backlight/%k/brightness", RUN+="/usr/bin/chmod g+w /sys/class/backlight/%k/brightness"
// The Hub's Machine page flips the hardware GPU MUX through
// `ryoku-gpu-mux set <mode>`, which writes a root-owned firmware knob. The
// switch itself is already the user's deliberate act (a click on a named
// control, and the knob only takes effect after a reboot the user confirms),
// so a passwordless grant keeps the GUI path from needing a terminal; the
// grant is scoped to the one program for an active local wheel user. The
// helper validates its own argument: `set` accepts only hybrid|discrete, and
// the value written to the knob is derived from that closed pair, so nothing
// arbitrary reaches the firmware file.
polkit.addRule(function (action, subject) {
if (action.id === "org.freedesktop.policykit.exec" &&
action.lookup("program") === "/usr/bin/ryoku-gpu-mux" &&
subject.local && subject.active && subject.isInGroup("wheel")) {
return polkit.Result.YES;
# 90-ryoku-gpu.rules
# managed by Ryoku (system/hardware/gpu). per PCI GPU, drop a boot-stable,
# colon-free /dev/dri/ryoku-gpu-<pci-slot> symlink so Hyprland's AQ_DRM_DEVICES
# can pin the strongest GPU as primary.
# why: AQ_DRM_DEVICES uses ':' as its separator, so the colon-laden
# /dev/dri/by-path names are out, and bare /dev/dri/cardN renumbers across
# boots. key the symlink on the PCI slot and swap its ':' and '.' for '-':
# token build: %p = the device devpath
# (/devices/.../0000:01:00.0/drm/card1). first sed drops the /drm/cardN tail,
# second sed keeps the trailing path component (the PCI slot), tr maps ':' and
# '.' to '-'. %c = that program's output. KERNELS limits the rule to GPUs whose
# parent is a PCI device, so the slot is always there.
SUBSYSTEM=="drm", KERNEL=="card[0-9]*", KERNELS=="????:??:??.?", PROGRAM="/bin/sh -c 'echo %p | sed s#/drm/.*## | sed s#.*/## | tr :. -'", SYMLINK+="dri/ryoku-gpu-%c"
# Ryoku: grant the active-seat user an ACL on a QMK/VIA keyboard's raw HID node
# so qmk_hid can drive its RGB matrix (theme-following keyboard lighting) without
# root. ryoku-hw-qmk matches only VIA control interfaces (usage page 0xFF60), so
# this never opens up unrelated hidraw devices. Numbered before 73-seat-late,
# which reads the uaccess tag and applies the ACL.
SUBSYSTEM=="hidraw", PROGRAM="/usr/bin/ryoku-hw-qmk %S%p", TAG+="uaccess"
# Ryoku: the shell's keypress overlay (the keycast shown while recording) reads
# keyboard evdev devices through the daemon. Grant the active-seat user an ACL on
# keyboards via uaccess so the feature works without the broad `input` group,
# which grants raw keyboard access on every seat and bypasses Wayland's input
# isolation. Scoped to keyboards; runs after 60-input-id sets the tag and before
# 73-seat-late applies the ACL (see the file number).
SUBSYSTEM=="input", ENV{ID_INPUT_KEYBOARD}=="1", TAG+="uaccess"
// Wi-Fi regulatory-domain pin (so 5 GHz is usable), authorized without a
// password so setting the country stays one click, matching the other network
// rules. Scoped to exactly /usr/bin/ryoku-wifi-regdom for an active local user
// in the wheel group. The helper only accepts a two-letter country code, which
// it validates, so a passwordless grant is safe.
polkit.addRule(function (action, subject) {
if (action.id === "org.freedesktop.policykit.exec" &&
action.lookup("program") === "/usr/bin/ryoku-wifi-regdom" &&
subject.local && subject.active && subject.isInGroup("wheel")) {
return polkit.Result.YES;
// Game Mode's WiFi power-save helper, authorized without a password so the deck
// toggle stays one click. Scoped to exactly /usr/bin/ryoku-wifi-powersave for an
// active local user in the wheel group. The helper only toggles 802.11 power-save
// (a benign radio power-management setting) and takes no arbitrary input, so a
// passwordless grant is safe.
polkit.addRule(function (action, subject) {
if (action.id === "org.freedesktop.policykit.exec" &&
action.lookup("program") === "/usr/bin/ryoku-wifi-powersave" &&
subject.local && subject.active && subject.isInGroup("wheel")) {
return polkit.Result.YES;
// Network panel DNS switch, authorized without a password so the provider
// buttons apply in one click. Scoped to any ryoku-dns helper (basename match, so
// a dev checkout's non-/usr/bin path still authorizes) for an active local user
// in the wheel group. The helper only writes a NetworkManager
// global-dns drop-in (a fixed provider list or validated addresses) and reverts
// to DHCP, the same network control NetworkManager already grants the active
// user, so a passwordless grant is safe.
polkit.addRule(function (action, subject) {
if (action.id === "org.freedesktop.policykit.exec" &&
/(^|\/)ryoku-dns$/.test(action.lookup("program")) &&
subject.local && subject.active && subject.isInGroup("wheel")) {
return polkit.Result.YES;
// NetworkManager Wi-Fi backend switch (Settings -> Connections), authorized
// without a password so the toggle stays one click, matching the DNS switch.
// Scoped to exactly /usr/bin/ryoku-wifi-backend for an active local user in the
// wheel group. The helper only ever selects iwd or wpa_supplicant and takes no
// arbitrary input, so a passwordless grant is safe.
polkit.addRule(function (action, subject) {
if (action.id === "org.freedesktop.policykit.exec" &&
action.lookup("program") === "/usr/bin/ryoku-wifi-backend" &&
subject.local && subject.active && subject.isInGroup("wheel")) {
return polkit.Result.YES;
// The kill switch exposes only four fixed actions; the helper rejects every
// other argument and never executes caller-provided commands. Grant this exact
// program to the active local wheel user so a cutoff is still possible when a
// network problem prevents an authentication round-trip.
polkit.addRule(function (action, subject) {
if (action.id === "org.freedesktop.policykit.exec" &&
action.lookup("program") === "/usr/bin/ryoku-network-kill" &&
subject.local && subject.active && subject.isInGroup("wheel")) {
return polkit.Result.YES;
// ryoku-power's login-time `apply` re-applies the stored battery charge ceiling
// and PCIe ASPM policy (both root-owned sysfs writes that do not survive a
// reboot), authorized without a password so autostart never blocks on a prompt.
// Scoped to exactly /usr/bin/ryoku-power for an active local user in the wheel
// group. Unlike the WiFi power-save helper this one does take an argument, but
// the passwordless grant stays safe because it is a closed, validated set: the
// charge limit is range-checked to an integer 50-100, and the ASPM policy is
// rejected unless it is one the kernel itself currently offers, so nothing
// arbitrary ever reaches the privileged write.
polkit.addRule(function (action, subject) {
if (action.id === "org.freedesktop.policykit.exec" &&
action.lookup("program") === "/usr/bin/ryoku-power" &&
subject.local && subject.active && subject.isInGroup("wheel")) {
return polkit.Result.YES;
// Game Mode's system-level tuning (ryoku-game-tune) flips root-owned knobs that
// need no password prompt, because the panel toggle is one click and a prompt
// mid-session would make it useless: deep CPU idle states, the NMI watchdog,
// split/bus-lock mitigation, and three VM knobs, all saved and restored exactly.
// Scoped to exactly /usr/bin/ryoku-game-tune for an active local user in the
// wheel group.
// The passwordless grant stays safe because nothing the caller says reaches a
// write. The argument set is closed to three fixed verbs (apply, restore,
// status), every value written is a constant compiled into the helper, and the
// paths are fixed sysfs and /proc/sys locations. There is no argument that makes
// it write an arbitrary value to an arbitrary file.
polkit.addRule(function (action, subject) {
if (action.id === "org.freedesktop.policykit.exec" &&
action.lookup("program") === "/usr/bin/ryoku-game-tune" &&
subject.local && subject.active && subject.isInGroup("wheel")) {
return polkit.Result.YES;
# systemd keeps NvPCRs (TPM NV indexes it extends with the hardware, product
# and login measurements) only on a box whose UKI is signed with a PCR key:
# setting one up needs tpm2-pcr-public-key.pem. Ryoku's UKIs are unsigned, so
# every boot failed systemd-tpm2-setup-early, systemd-pcrproduct and each
# systemd-pcrlogin@ on "No such file or directory". TPM2_BROKEN_NVPCR is
# systemd's own switch for a TPM without usable NvPCRs: the setup skips them
# and the measurement units exit cleanly. A box that does carry the key keeps
# its NvPCRs.
SUBSYSTEM=="tpmrm", KERNEL=="tpmrm[0-9]*", \
TEST!="/etc/systemd/tpm2-pcr-public-key.pem", \
TEST!="/run/systemd/tpm2-pcr-public-key.pem", \
TEST!="/usr/lib/systemd/tpm2-pcr-public-key.pem", \
TEST!="/.extra/tpm2-pcr-public-key.pem", \
ENV{TPM2_BROKEN_NVPCR}="1"
// Ryoku: let the active desktop user (in the wheel group) set the system time
// zone without a password prompt, so the world-map picker in Settings > Global
// applies instantly. Scoped to the single timedate1 set-timezone action; no
// other privilege is granted. Installed to /usr/share/polkit-1/rules.d/ by the
// ryoku-desktop package.
polkit.addRule(function (action, subject) {
if (action.id === "org.freedesktop.timedate1.set-timezone" &&
subject.active && subject.isInGroup("wheel")) {
return polkit.Result.YES;
// The argv1 annotation selects this action only for the typed users API; the
// helper validates every later argument again after crossing the root boundary.
polkit.addRule(function (action, subject) {
if (action.id === "dev.ryoku.users.manage" &&
action.lookup("program") === "/usr/bin/ryoku-host" &&
subject.local && subject.active) {
return polkit.Result.AUTH_ADMIN_KEEP;
